wave.summary: Fixed the Notices queue losing its cursor on drill-down round trips without touching App.tsx or useKeyboardNav (both frozen). AttentionQueue.tsx now persists the active row's repoId to sessionStorage (keyed 'atlas-notices-selection', with a module-level fallback if storage throws) whenever the keyboard cursor moves, and restores it on mount by locating that repoId in the current rows (falling back to index 0 if the repo is gone or on first-ever mount), pushing it into useKeyboardNav via its own setActiveIndex since the hook has no initial-index param. A subtlety surfaced during TDD: the pre-existing test 'drills down on click and on j / Enter keyboard navigation' clicks row 2 (tide-tables), goes Back, then does j+Enter expecting to land on field-notes (row 1) — i.e. it assumes the cursor reset to 0 after a click-driven drill-down. Persisting on every cursor change (including clicks) breaks that assertion, which I was told not to modify. Resolved by scoping persistence to keyboard-driven cursor movement only (j/k, and the restore itself) — a click still drills in and still visually highlights the clicked row for the instant before navigation, but doesn't move/persist the cursor, since a click is a direct action rather than a cursor placement. This keeps the old test's semantics (click-drill-then-Back-then-j starts fresh at row 0) while satisfying the acceptance criterion for the keyboard round trip (taste finding: 'j+Enter round-trips all reopened the same repo'). Added a new mount test in Overview.test.tsx: renders Overview, presses j j (cursor to tide-tables), unmounts, remounts, and asserts the restored active row is tide-tables (not row 0), then that a further j advances to old-survey (the next row) — proving the cursor genuinely continued rather than restarting. No existing assertions were modified. Full suite: 209/209 passing across 10 files (node_modules was untracked; symlinked from /Users/truman/Projects/repo-atlas/node_modules before running npm test, per the conductor note).
